# AF 第四章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 4

[P01] By late summer the news of what had happened on Animal Farm had spread across half the county（县）. Every day Snowball and Napoleon sent out pigeons to mingle（混合） with the animals on neighbouring farms, tell them the story of the uprising（起义）, and teach them the tune of 'animals of England'. Most of this time Mr. Jones spent sitting in the taproom（酒吧间） of the Red Lion at Willingdon, complaining to anyone who would listen of the monstrous（可怕的） injustice（不公） of being turned out of his property（财产） by a pack of good-for-nothing animals. The other farmers sympathised（同情） but did not at first give him much help.

[P02] Deep down, each was secretly wondering whether he could turn Jones's bad luck to his own good. It was lucky that the owners of the two farms next to Animal Farm were always on bad terms. One, named Foxwood（狐林）, was a large, neglected（被忽视）, old-fashioned farm, much overgrown（杂草丛生） by woodland（林地）, with pastures（牧场） worn out and hedges（树篱） in a shameful（可耻） state. Its owner, Mr. Pilkington, was an easy-going gentleman farmer who spent most of his time fishing or hunting according to the season. The other, called Pinchfield（窄地）, was smaller and better kept. Its owner was Mr. Frederick, a tough（艰难）, shrewd（精明） man, always involved（卷入） in lawsuits（诉讼） and known for driving hard bargains（交易）.

[P03] These two disliked（讨厌） each other so much that they could not agree on anything, even to protect their own interests. Taproom Monstrous Property Pack turn Jones's misfortune（不幸） to his own advantage. Adjoin（毗连） On bad terms Shrewd Perpetual（永久） Drive hard bargains Nevertheless（然而）, both were deeply frightened by the uprising on Animal Farm, and very eager（渴望） to stop their own animals from learning too much about it. At first they pretended to laugh at the idea of animals running a farm themselves. The whole thing would be over in a fortnight（两周）, they said. They spread it around that the animals on the farm (they insisted on calling it the farm Farm; they would not accept the name "Animal Farm") were always fighting among themselves and were quickly starving（挨饿） to death.

[P04] As time went on and the animals clearly had not starved（饿死） to death, Frederick and Pilkington changed their tune and began to talk of the terrible wickedness（邪恶） that now flourished（兴旺） on Animal Farm. It was said that the animals there practised cannibalism（同类相食）, tortured（折磨） one another with red-hot horseshoes（马蹄铁）, and shared their females. This was what came of rebelling（反叛） against the laws of Nature, Frederick and Pilkington said.

However, these stories were never fully believed. Rumours of a wonderful farm, where the human beings had been driven out and the animals managed their own affairs, continued to spread in vague and twisted forms, and all through that year a wave of rebelliousness ran through the countryside.

[P05] Bulls（公牛） that had always been easy to control suddenly turned wild. Sheep broke down hedges and ate the clover. Cows kicked over the pail（桶）. Hunters（猎人） refused their fences and threw their riders（骑手） to the other side. Above all, the tune and even the words of 'Beasts（野兽） of England' were known everywhere. It spread with amazing speed. The human beings could not hold their anger when they heard this song, though they pretended to think it was funny. They could not understand, they said, how animals could sing such shameful rubbish. Any animal caught singing it was whipped on the spot（地点）. And yet the song could not be stopped.

[P06] The blackbirds（黑鸟） whistled（吹哨） it in the hedges, the pigeons cooed（咕咕叫） it in the elms（榆树）, it mixed into the noise of the smithies（铁匠铺） and the tune of the church bells. And when the human beings heard it, they secretly shook with fear, hearing in it a prophecy（预言） of their future doom（厄运）. Early in October, when the corn was cut and stacked（堆叠） and some of it was already threshed（打谷）, a flight of pigeons came whirling（旋转） through the air and landed in the yard of Animal Farm in the wildest excitement.

[P07] Jones and all his men, with half a dozen others from Foxwood and Pinchfield, had entered the five-barred（阻挡） gate and were coming up the cart-track that led to the farm. They all carried sticks, except Jones, who marched ahead with a gun in his hands. Clearly they were going to try to take back the farm. This had long been expected, and all preparations（准备） had been made. Snowball, who had studied an old book of Julius Caesar's campaigns which he had found in the farmhouse（农舍）, was in charge（冲锋） of the defensive operations. He gave his orders quickly, and in a couple of minutes every animal was at his post. As the human beings came near the farm buildings, Snowball launched his first attack.

[P08] All thirty-five pigeons flew to and fro（来回） over the men's heads and dropped on them from mid-air; while the men dealt（处理） with this, the geese, hiding behind the hedge（树篱）, rushed out and pecked（啄） viciously（恶毒地） at their legs. However, this was only a light skirmishing（小冲突） move to create a little disorder（混乱）, and the men easily drove the geese off with sticks. Snowball now launched his second attack. Muriel, Benjamin, and all the sheep, with Snowball at the head, rushed forward and prodded（戳） and butted the men from every side, while Benjamin turned and lashed（鞭打） at them with his small hoofs（蹄）.

[P09] But once again the men, with their sticks and their hobnailed（钉鞋） boots, were too strong for them; and suddenly, at a squeal（尖叫） from Snowball, which was the signal（信号） to retreat（撤退）, all the animals turned and fled through the gateway（入口） into the yard. The men gave a shout of triumph（胜利）. They saw, as they imagined, their enemies running away, and they rushed after them in disorder. This was just what Snowball had intended. As soon as they were well inside the yard, the three horses, the three cows, and the rest of the pigs, who had been lying（躺） in ambush（埋伏） in the cowshed（牛棚）, suddenly came out behind them, cutting them off.

[P10] Snowball gave the signal to charge. He dashed（猛冲） straight at Jones. Jones saw him, raised his gun and fired. The pellets（颗粒） made bloody（血腥） streaks（条纹） along Snowball's back, and a sheep dropped dead. Without stopping, Snowball threw his fifteen stone（石头） against Jones's legs. Jones fell into a pile of dung（粪便） and his gun flew out of his hands. But the most terrifying（可怕） sight was Boxer, standing on his hind（后面的） legs and hitting out with his great iron-shod（装蹄） hoofs like a stallion（种马）. His first blow hit a stable-lad（马童） from Foxwood on the skull（头骨） and stretched（伸展） him lifeless（无生命） in the mud.

[P11] At the sight, several men dropped their sticks and ran. Panic took them, and the next moment all the animals were chasing（追赶） them round the yard. They were gored（刺伤）, kicked, bitten, stepped on. There was not an animal that did not take vengeance（复仇） after his own fashion. Even the cat leapt（跳跃） off a roof onto a cowman（牛夫）'s shoulders and sank her claws（爪子） in his neck, at which he yelled（喊叫） horribly（可怕地）. When the opening was clear, the men were glad to rush out of the yard and make a bolt（逃跑） for the main road.

[P12] And so within five minutes of their invasion（入侵） they were in ignominious（可耻的） retreat by the same way as they had come, with a flock（羊群） of geese hissing after them and pecking（啄） at their calves（小牛） all the way. Flight ambush cowshed rear（后部） cut them off charge pellet（弹丸） score score bloody streaks drop dead halt（停止） fling（扔） hurl（猛投） stone =14lb≈95kg dung spectacle（景象） rear iron-shod stallion stable-lad take sb on the skull stretch（伸展） him lifeless in the mud panic overtakes（追上） them gore（刺伤） trample（踩踏） on after his own fashion sink her teeth in at which he yelled the opening was clear bolt ignominious. All the men were gone except one. Back in the yard Boxer was pawing（刨地） with his hoof（蹄） at the stable-lad who lay face down in the mud, trying to turn him over.

[P13] The boy did not move. "He is dead," said Boxer sadly. "I did not mean to do that. I forgot I was wearing iron shoes. Who will believe I did not do this on purpose?" "No sentimentality（感伤）, comrade（同志）!" cried Snowball, whose wounds were still dripping（滴落） blood. "War is war. The only good human being is a dead one." "I do not wish to take life, not even human life," Boxer said again with tears in his eyes, "Where is Mollie?""Where is Mollie?" cried somebody. Mollie was in fact missing. For a moment there was great alarm; it was feared that the men might have hurt her in some way, or even carried her off with them.

[P14] In the end, however, she was found hiding in her stall（畜栏） with her head buried in the hay（干草） in the manger（食槽）. She had run away as soon as the gun went off. And when the others came back from looking for her, they found that the stable-lad（马童）, who was in fact only stunned（震惊）, had already recovered（恢复） and run off. The animals had now come together again in the wildest excitement, each telling his own brave deeds（事迹） in the battle at the top of his voice. A celebration（庆祝） of the victory was held at once. The flag was run up and 'animals of England' was sung many times, then the sheep who had been killed was given a solemn（庄严） funeral, a hawthorn（山楂） bush being planted on her grave（坟墓）.

[P15] At the graveside（墓边） Snowball made a short speech, stressing that all animals must be ready to die for Animal Farm if need be. The animals agreed with one mind to create a military（军事） honour, "Animal Hero, First Class," which was given right there and then to Snowball and Boxer. It was a brass（黄铜） medal (they were really some old horse-brasses（铜牌） found in the harness（马具）-room), to be worn on Sundays and holidays. There was also "Animal Hero, Second Class," which was given after death to the dead sheep. There was much talk about what the battle should be called.

[P16] In the end, they named it the Battle of the Cowshed, because that was where the ambush had started. Jones's gun was found lying in the mud, and they knew there was a supply of cartridges（弹药） in the farmhouse. They decided to set the gun up at the foot of the Flagstaff（旗杆）, like a piece of artillery（大炮）, and to fire it twice a year--once on October the twelfth, the anniversary（周年） of the Battle of the Cowshed, and once on Midsummer（仲夏） Day, the anniversary of the uprising.
